rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Apply the fundamental laws of classical mechanics to investigate and assess physical phenomena that impact society.
Use mathematics up to and including calculus to solve classical mechanics problems.
Communicate physics concepts, processes, and results effectively.

rows.title: Waves and Thermodynamics for Scientists and Engineers
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Apply the fundamental laws of waves and thermodynamics to investigate and assess physical phenomena that impact society.
Use mathematics up to and including calculus to solve waves and thermodynamics problems.
Communicate physics concepts, processes, and results effectively.

rows.title: Elementary Filipino (Tagalog)
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Interpret spoken and written Filipino (Tagalog) at the elementary level.
Write short communications incorporating the main markers and verb inflections of the Filipino (Tagalog) language.
Communicate orally in basic everyday situations using a range of Filipino (Tagalog) grammatical structures with accurate pronunciation and intonation.
Explain elements of Philippine culture at an appropriate level for a basic beginning Filipino (Tagalog) language learner.
Use Filipino expressions to indicate respect or formality in various situations.

rows.title: Government & Politics of Latin America
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Compare the political systems, ideologies, and governments in Latin America.
Examine the political economy of Latin America and its impact on society, including external influences, and U.S. interactions.
Critique the role of Latin America's international relations with the US and other countries.
Assess the role of important political forces in Latin America.
Analyze comparative political systems and government institutions as well as cultural components in shaping these systems.

rows.title: Political Theory
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Apply the study of political theory to political life, political institutions, and important political phenomena, including issues of identity.
Analyze political theory through diverse foundational texts reflecting political values and beliefs across time and cultures.
Assess the origins of political theories, ancient, modern, and contemporary in the historical and social contexts surrounding them.
Explain the defining elements and assumptions of major political theories and ideologies, especially liberalism and conservatism.

rows.title: Middle East Governments and Politics
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Evaluate the structure and functioning of the governments and political systems in the Middle East and North Africa.
Assess current political issues, events, and actors in the Middle East.
Identify and compare the human rights conditions of ethnic, racial, and religious minority groups, women, and LGBT persons across the countries of the Middle East.
Analyze Middle East governments and politics by selecting and using appropriate comparative Political Science methodologies and approaches, including the use of primary sources.

rows.title: Theories of Personality
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Describe and apply basic terms and definitions in personality psychology
Evaluate the methods of studying personality
Describe and evaluate the intersectionality of culture, race, and/or gender in personality theory
Compare major personality theories
Apply the major personality theories to explain the personalities of self and/or others

rows.title: Biological Psychology
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Describe the central features of neuroanatomy, neurophysiology, and the endocrine system and their relationship to psychological phenomena.
Apply basic terms and concepts used in biological psychology.
Apply different levels of analysis including biological, cognitive, sociocultural, and theoretical to explain normal and abnormal psychological behaviors and mental processes.
Evaluate current research design and findings in biological psychology.

rows.title: Queer Psychology
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Explain distinctions among various sexual and gender minorities.
Apply current theories and empirical research to sexual orientation and gender diversity.
Analyze the social construction of sexual orientation and gender.
Evaluate the causes of stigma and their impact on sexual and gender minorities.

rows.title: Forensic Psychology
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Describe how psychologists influence the legal process through research, expert testimony, and as consultants and practitioners.
Compare the methods and goals of psychology and the legal system.
Evaluate psychological research, theory, practice, and methodology as applied to a legal issue.
Analyze landmark court decisions and the underlying assumptions about behavior.
Analyze the opposing arguments of psycholegal issues in an objective way.

rows.title: Psychology of Stress
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Differentiate between types of acute and chronic stress.
Interpret stress physiology and how stress impacts physical and mental health.
Analyze circumstances that influence stress reactivity and life satisfaction.
Describe and apply both active and palliative coping strategies for stress.

rows.title: Fire Training Work Experience II
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Apply Firefighter I knowledge and skills to emergency and non-emergency situations.
Analyze dangerous situations and assist with retrieving appropriate tools and equipment for fire personnel.
Use tools and equipment according to the National Fire Protection Association's Standard 1001 for Firefighter I.
Explain the importance of teamwork at emergency incidents and non-emergency training.
Assess patients and use appropriate medical protocols in a firefighter response situation.

rows.title: Firefighter One Academy
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Execute job knowledge and performance specific to the State Fire Training Firefighter One curriculum for firefighting and rescue
Execute job knowledge and performance specific to the State Fire Training Firefighter One curriculum for wildland fire fighting
Execute job knowledge and performance specific to the State Fire Training Firefighter One curriculum for hazardous materials
Execute job knowledge and performance specific to the State Fire Training Firefighter Two curriculum for firefighting and rescue

rows.title: Fire Service Career Preparation
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Identify fields of interest or career paths within fire service organizations and develop a plan for self-study and group study.
Describe educational and vocational training resources related to the fire service as part of a career educational plan to prepare for the fire service application process.
Locate entry-level fire service job announcements and employment opportunities.
Articulate the three major components of the fire service entrance exams and key areas of study for each component.

rows.title: Fire Protection Equipment & Systems
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Identify the chemistry and physics of fire behavior relevant to fire protection equipment and systems.
Describe the principles and characteristics of fire detection and alarm systems and fire equipment and suppression systems.
Explain the effects of smoke control management systems in buildings.
Explain the various fire protection and detection systems within a building that contribute to fire and life safety.

rows.title: Introduction to Fire Prevention
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Analyze fire prevention efforts as they relate to fire loss data.
Examine the need, responsibilities, and importance of fire prevention for public and private fire prevention organizations.
Classify minimum professional qualifications and training at the state and national level for fire inspectors, fire investigators, and public educators.
Differentiate the elements of a new project construction plan review program.
Distinguish laws, rules, codes, and other regulations relevant to fire protection and the authority having jurisdiction.

rows.title: Hazardous Materials First Responder Operations
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Analyze the chemical and physical properties of hazardous materials and the health hazards associated with chemical releases.
Interpret the key components and use of the Emergency Response Guidebook.
Evaluate protective equipment and measures to be taken during a hazardous materials incident.

rows.title: Company Officer 2D: All-Risk Command Operations
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Develop and implement an incident action plan involving single and multi-unit operations that might include a fire incident or non-fire incident.

Complete incident command form 201 that employs principles of command, resource management, emergency operations, scene conditions, local emergency plans, local evacuation, allocation of resources, and evaluation of fire behavior.
Implement a plan of action for emergencies based on the National Fire Protections Standard 1600 for disasters, emergency, and business continuity plans.
Manage a post-analysis of an emergency incident that lists the elements, describes the events that occurred, and suggests actions in similar future incidents.

rows.title: Intro to Social Work and Human Services
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Discuss the historical evolution and current state of social welfare and human services in the United States.
Explain the current service delivery system environment that addresses social work and human service clients’ needs.
Analyze contemporary social issues that impact social welfare and human service agencies and institutions.
Describe the ethical responsibilities of working with social work and human service organizations with attention to cultural humility and oppressed groups.
Explain the research methods used to inform and evaluate social work practice.

rows.title: Introduction to Research Methods
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Analyze the complexities of research ethics in scientific inquiry.
Apply quantitative and qualitative research methods to examine sociological questions.
Explain and use basic descriptive and inferential statistical analyses.
Compare how theories, concepts, and hypotheses are employed in qualitative and quantitative research designs.

rows.title: Men, Masculinity, and Society
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Identify and apply theories and research methods in the study of masculinities in culture and society.
Compare key intersectional frameworks that influence the perceptions and experiences of masculinity in social contexts.
Analyze the major social institutions and practices that construct masculine roles and how these constructions interact with one another.
Assess how the sociological perspective contributes to the understanding of accepted masculinity’s power to create difference and inequality

rows.title: Beginning Conversational Spanish
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Apply intelligible pronunciation and intonation at a novice level when talking about personal or university-life situations.
Use accurate grammatical structures in Spanish at a novice level to describe people, places, and things, or to express likes and dislikes.
Respond effectively to spoken Spanish with appropriate grammatical forms, accurate vocabulary, and clear pronunciation at a novice level.
Communicate in Spanish in an appropriate and effective manner on cultural topics related to the evolution of the language or family and community traditions in the Spanish-speaking world.

rows.title: Elementary Spanish
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Communicate effectively in Spanish at a novice-mid level with accurate grammatical structure, intelligible pronunciation and intonation
Interpret the main ideas and grammatical forms of a written text in Spanish at a novice-mid level
Compose short written communications in Spanish incorporating the principles of present tense syntax at the novice-mid level
Articulate aspects of the cultures of the Spanish-speaking world areas and communities

rows.title: Grammar Review and Composition
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Use complex structures to interact orally in Spanish and synthesize information with near-native fluency.
Apply editing skills to revise Spanish errors in grammar, punctuation, and word usage.
Summarize and organize arguments effectively with near-native fluency.
Explain select cultural, social and political issues in the Spanish-speaking world.

rows.title: Intermediate Spanish
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Communicate in Spanish at an intermediate-high level with accurate grammatical structure, intelligible pronunciation, and intonation.
Interpret the main ideas of a written text in Spanish at an intermediate-high level
Compose short written communications incorporating the principles of past and present syntax in indicative and subjunctive modes at a intermediate-high level.
Articulate aspects of Latin American and Spanish Peninsular cultures at an intermediate-high level.

rows.title: Spanish for Heritage Speakers 2
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Analyze and synthesize Spanish grammar structures and syntax rules using linguistic knowledge to infer spelling, time frames, and sentence construction.

Communicate in writing with enriched Spanish vocabulary and complex syntax producing full paragraphs that are organized and detailed, providing a well-supported argument, without interference with English.
Express thoughts efficiently on topics of personal and community interest using a broad range of vocabulary and high-frequency structures.
Compare cultural aspects of Spanish-speaking countries of the Andean and Southern Cone regions.

rows.title: Intermediate Spanish
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Communicate in Spanish at an intermediate-high level with accurate grammatical structure, intelligible pronunciation, and intonation.
Interpret the main ideas of a written text in Spanish at an intermediate-high level.
Compose short written communications incorporating the principles of past and present syntax in indicative and subjunctive modes at a intermediate-high level.
Articulate aspects of Latin American and Spanish Peninsular cultures at an intermediate-high level.

rows.title: Continuation of Intermediate Spanish
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Converse on diverse topics expressing personal ideas demonstrating language fluency at the intermediate-advanced level.
Interpret written texts on a variety of personal, cultural or social topics at an intermediate-advanced level.
Compose written texts using complex grammar structures, accurate syntax and punctuation on a variety of personal, cultural or social topics at the intermediate-advanced level.
Analyze at an intermediate-advanced level historical and cultural elements and issues from the Spanish-speaking world to interpret and describe societal differences and diverse viewpoints.

rows.title: Introduction to Statistics
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Assess how data were collected and recognize how data collection affects what conclusions can be drawn from the data.
Identify appropriate graphs and summary statistics for variables and relationships between them and correctly interpret information from graphs and summary statistics.
Describe and apply probability concepts and distributions.
Demonstrate an understanding of, and ability to use, basic ideas of statistical processes, including hypothesis tests and confidence interval estimation.
Identify appropriate statistical techniques and use technology-based statistical analysis to describe, interpret, and communicate results.
Evaluate ethical issues in statistical practice.

rows.title: Orientation to Visual Media Design
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Research and discuss career opportunities in visual communication fields
Identify a degree or certificate program in Visual Media Design that would support career goals
Assess resources for academic success and career search in visual communication fields

rows.title: History of Graphic Design
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Identify significant movements in graphic design history.
Analyze and interpret images, symbols, and typography historically used in visual communication, using design language.
Evaluate the influence of technological, commercial and societal factors on graphic design work.

rows.title: Graphic Design II
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Design and develop solutions for a range of interactive and complex print projects.
Analyze and critically discuss the strengths and weaknesses of interactive and static design solutions.
Present and document an iterative design process.

rows.title: User Experience
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Employ industry-standard tools used in User Experience design.
Employ UX design process models in developing design solutions.
Present and justify design decisions using relevant User Experience design concepts and vocabulary.
Critique user experience design verbally and in writing.

rows.title: Web Production II
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Design responsive web content using industry best practices
Critique and discuss responsive projects in terms of usability and accessibility
Employ an iterative design process to produce a responsive web project

rows.title: Adobe InDesign: Publication Design
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Construct complex multi-page documents following industry best practices for layout and typesetting.
Use an iterative design process to create professional-level publications using Adobe InDesign.
Assess design solutions and articulate their strengths and weaknesses.

rows.title: Visual Development for Animation
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Describe the various development processes involved in visual development for animation
Design and illustrate scenery for an animation or game
Conceptualize and illustrate original characters for animation
Create a storyboard based upon a script or narrative

rows.title: Professional Practice
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Summarize basic legal issues relating to the visual media design profession.
Describe the difference between working as a design freelancer, running a small design firm, and working as a designer for an employer.
Prepare a complete project bid for a visual media design project.

rows.title: Nurse Assistant/Convalescent Care
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Identify the signs and symptoms to be reported of various diseases, disorders, and behaviors among the elderly.
Explain the legal rules and guidelines set by Title 22 and Title 42.
Describe the professional and ethical roles and responsibilities of the nursing assistant.
Describe and report various types of elder abuse.
Perform geriatric and other long term care related to activities of daily living.

rows.title: Basic Medical/Surgical Nursing
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Differentiate health and illness across the life span and understand the impact of culture on health for appropriate nursing care.
Identify and discuss with geriatric clients the processes and nursing implications of normal aging, death, and physiological and psychological changes.
Apply knowledge of the anatomy and physiology of the gastrointestinal, integumentary, and musculoskeletal systems to identification and nursing interventions for various related disorders.
Compare and evaluate various diagnostic and laboratory tests and provide nursing measures in relation to the test results.
Describe LVN licensure exam expectations and the critical thinking, clinical judgment, and Next Generation NCLEX-PN skills needed for success.

rows.title: Intermediate Adult Medical Surgical Nursing
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Formulate daily nursing care in response to a range of major medical-surgical disease conditions and apply appropriate nursing interventions to selected patients.
Apply intermediate-level nursing knowledge and critical thinking related to various medical-surgical disease conditions.
Apply intermediate-level nursing and appropriate clinical judgment in caring for diverse clients with different medical-surgical disorders.
Manage safe, intermediate-level nursing care for patients with a wide range of medical surgical disorders.

rows.title: Clinical and Skills Lab III
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Describe and analyze at least ten (10) of the LVN Department's Standard Steps of Nursing Procedures.
Assemble the appropriate equipment for each obstetric, pediatric, and medical-surgical skill performed, utilizing standard steps for each procedure.
Explain the purpose of each obstetric, pediatric, and medical-surgical skill performed and formulate a related patient teaching plan.
Perform assessment of patients of all ages with a variety of obstetric, pediatric, medical-surgical conditions and assessment of community health needs in diverse healthcare settings.
Perform, discuss, and identify appropriate health needs and teaching based on client assessment in community and clinical settings.

rows.title: Introduction to Women's and Gender Studies: Feminism Demystified
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Examine gender, feminism, and women’s studies through an intersectional lens.
Apply feminist theory to social, political, and economic issues.
Evaluate the causes, effects, and systemic structures contributing to gender-based violence
Define, assess, and propose feminist approaches to social change, emphasizing practical applications and community engagement.
